Blocking contract finding before landing this rewrite: the generated `McpToolResult` API promises top-level `content`, `structuredContent`, and `isError`, but the current bridge returns the internal `AgentToolResult` envelope instead (`structuredContent` under `details` and failures only as `details.status: "error"`). The installed MCP SDK and Codex Code Mode both preserve the advertised top-level shape, including resolved `isError: true` tool failures.

The existing MCP integration fixture does not cross the raw MCP materializer boundary, so its green result misses this mismatch. A production-boundary reproduction returns only `content` and `details`; the checked-in structured-content parsing pattern then fails against the actual materialized text.

The clean owner is the Code Mode MCP guest projection, not the shared MCP materializer or Tool Search. Project the final value to `{ content, structuredContent?, isError? }`, derive failure through the canonical tool-result classifier, and keep MCP failures as resolved values so guest code can recover. This needs to be resolved together with the existing persisted Cron-script compatibility/migration decision; removing `.details` without that decision is a shipped compatibility change.

Required proof before merge: real-materializer success and `isError: true` cases, no leaked internal metadata, unchanged Tool Search failure accounting, and one Gateway Code Mode MCP E2E for structured success plus resolved tool failure. Current head is also conflicting with `main`, so prior green checks do not establish a mergeable final result.
